guard: Appendix A of the language reference and CATALOG are two renderings of ONE table: the same codes, each exactly once, each carrying the title the code actually raises. A reader repairing a program searches the document for the title the tool printed, so a document that lists a code the code does not raise, or a title the code no longer says, sends that reader nowhere. (FAIL-FAST suite: markers are upstream of the cells they guard.)

mutations.name: a catalog title drifts from the row that renders it
mutations.find: L5024: "A recorded value has no canonical form",
mutations.replace: L5024: "A recorded value has no canonical shape",
mutations.completionMarker: ok Appendix A lists exactly the catalog's codes
mutations.cell: and every one of those 99 rows carries the title the code raises
mutations.note: The REAL drift, replayed. L5024's row read "A recorded binding has no canonical form" while the code raised "A recorded value has no canonical form" from 5e606152 to c38b2ee8, because the rule grew to cover a failure's detail and a scope's result and the row was left behind. The set cell cannot see this: the codes still match one for one. Only the title cell reds, which is why the two are not one conjunction.

mutations.name: the catalog loses a code the document still lists
mutations.find: L5021: "Resume over a journal without the run's pins",
mutations.expectRed: Appendix A lists exactly the catalog's codes
mutations.completionMarker: ok every js block in docs/workflows.md validates as written
mutations.cell: Appendix A lists exactly the catalog's codes, 99 of them, each once
mutations.note: The other direction, and the one a title comparison alone would miss: the document keeps a row whose code no longer exists. L5021 is chosen because no cell in this suite raises or names it, so the mutant reaches the set comparison rather than reding something upstream. The set cell runs BEFORE the title cell, so under this mutant it is the first red and the title cell never runs.
